brief:
Widows in Gaza are managing families without husbands while navigating acute shortages of shelter, water and education access, UN News reported. Women who lost spouses in the war now bear responsibility for basic survival tasks — securing food and housing, hauling water and keeping children enrolled in school — often from temporary tent accommodations. The economic and practical burden falls entirely on mothers already traumatized by loss.

Many widows lack regular income or family support networks as infrastructure across Gaza remains severely damaged. Schools operate sporadically, water systems have failed, and permanent housing is scarce, forcing displaced families to live in tents while women work multiple jobs to cover expenses.
dek: For women in Gaza who lost their husbands in the war, providing for a family no longer means just putting food on the table. Now it also means finding shelter, hauling water and keeping children in school – all from a tent.
title: Gaza's widows shoulder family survival alone amid war devastation
